$comment: Default settings seed for Aperture — R2 values (Docs 19-21). At runtime these live INSIDE the encrypted DB (doc 13 §6); this file is the first-run seed. [VERIFY] all model names / hotkeys / thresholds against the real target and current vendor docs (doc 00 conventions).

capture.$comment_default_state: Capture is OFF until the user opts in at first run (doc 13 §8).
capture.$comment_heartbeat: Adaptive heartbeat band (ADR-032/Q41): default 10 s, pulled toward the floor when event density is high and the ceiling when quiet.

loadout.$comment: L1 = Qwen2.5-VL-3B + faster-whisper small, co-residency CONDITIONAL on the 7.0 GB projection (ADR-030 — STT is the swap victim when it doesn't fit). L2 = Qwen2.5-VL-7B exclusive (opt-in, doc 04 §3).
loadout.$comment_vlm_download: Decision #30: the VLM weights are too big for the installer (NSIS 2 GB cap), so the Dashboard offers an explicit, user-click-only download (never automatic — no surprise network activity). URLs + byte sizes + sha256 are settings, never code (NG8); the destination file names come from SidecarConfig. SDLC review 2026-08-19 finding 5: the URLs are pinned to HF repo revision 5037fcf163dd95d1e41d1974465f0898ed108ca2 (resolve/main is a moving reference — a resumed .part against a re-uploaded file would pass the size check), and each artifact's sha256 (lowercase hex) is verified over the whole file once at download time before it is renamed into place. Size + sha256 verified against the ggml-org HF repo and the dev machine's files on 2026-08-22.
loadout.$comment_stt: What actually ships: whisper.cpp CPU+BLAS base.en (verified live 2026-08-14). The GPU path (faster-whisper/CTranslate2 or CUDA whisper.cpp) is still [VERIFY] with the SC4 gate — this key must name the model the app can really spawn, not an aspiration (2026-08-15 review).

voice.$comment_hotkey: NOT Ctrl+Win+Space: Windows reserves it for input-language switching (registration fails with multiple layouts).
voice.$comment_confidence: Decision #27: STT confidence below this floor shows the 'Did you say…?' confirm chip instead of acting. Clamped to [0,1] at read; 1.0 = always confirm. Read by the voice pipeline per utterance (no restart needed); edited live from the Dashboard Voice tab.

pattern_engine.$comment: Read by the pattern task at startup, on any set_settings write (decision #17's UI half — the Dashboard Advanced tab edits tau_conf / cold_start_support_floor / cooldown_min / cap_per_hour_default live), and on its daily maintenance tick as the backstop for edits made outside the app. Missing/invalid keys fall back to the crate constants in pattern-engine/src/config.rs — a typo can never weaken the engine.
pattern_engine.$comment_cap: Adaptive global cap 2-8/hr (ADR-032); the default is only the cold-start value.
pattern_engine.$comment_session_gap: Rolling idle-gap sessionizer (ADR-032): 15 min is the cold-start default; the learned gap clamps to 5-45 min.
pattern_engine.$comment_half_life: Split decay half-lives (ADR-033): temporal patterns ~5 d, sequence patterns ~14 d.

agent.$comment: v2 agent execution layer (Doc 22, wired 2026-08-22). step_cap = Q-V2-04's default (50, [PROVISIONAL] — owner to confirm), clamped 1-500; error_threshold = consecutive failed actions before the task fails (Doc 22 §3.3, clamped 1-20); confirm_low_confidence = pause for the user when Claude reports confidence:low (Doc 22 §5). Consequential-looking actions ALWAYS pause regardless (decisions #47/#51). Read at task start.

ui.$comment_dwell: Decision #7 (2026-08-16): now WIRED to the bubble's idle countdown (it was a compile-time constant) and editable from the Dashboard's Advanced tab. Clamped to 3-600 s by the overlay; a set_settings write applies to the next bubble, no restart.
ui.$comment_glass: ADR-039: at most 2 glass surfaces; the 3rd visible bubble renders in the opaque fallback class. Blur ceiling 12 px (doc 14 §2).
ui.$comment_freshness: Decision #5 (2026-08-16): half-life of the freshness factor in the bubble slot-admission score (score = confidence x 0.5^(age/half_life)), so a stale-but-confident queued bubble cannot block a fresher one forever. Settings-only on purpose — it tunes queue ordering, not anything visible. Clamped to 10-86400 s.

reasoning.$comment_transport: MCP-primary (ADR-025): Desktop MCP -> Claude CLI -> Messages API. Decision #39 (2026-08-16) keeps this default but makes switching trivial: the Dashboard's Advanced tab moves the preferred PUSH transport (CLI / Messages API) to the front, and set_settings REBUILDS the gateway in place, so the change is live on the next Send with no restart. MCP stays in the list either way — it is the pull route Claude Desktop uses and is never what a Send picks. If the default itself is ever flipped, amend ADR-025 (doc 19) + doc 09.
reasoning.$comment_scoped_allow: ADR-026 scoped always-allow was never implemented in v1 — the dead scoped_allow_* keys were removed (2026-08-15 review) so settings only advertise built behavior. Scoped allow returns with v2's per-task approval (Doc 22 §4.1).
reasoning.$comment_model: Claude model id + any beta headers are settings, never code (locked NG8). claude-opus-5 verified current as of 2026-08-13.

connectors.$comment: Per-connector staleness TTLs (decision #37, 2026-08-16: video goes stale fast, documents/IDE files stay resumable long). Code carries these as constants in crates/connectors — these keys are informational until a settings-load pass wires overrides; kept here so the tunables are visible in one place.
connectors.$comment_extension: Browser extension feed (ADR-027/028): native messaging (stdio + named pipe), no sockets. Toggle OFF halts forwarding (FIX 2.1); extension URLs run the same exclusion pipeline (FIX 2.2).
connectors.$comment_media: media_state coalescing [ASSUMPTION]: publish on video/state change, >=15 s position delta, or 30 s silence; pause/hidden always report exactly.

privacy.$comment_exclusions: Decision #20 (amends ADR-029/Q15): curated defaults (password managers, banking patterns — SHIPPED_DEFAULT_RULES in crates/capture/src/exclusion.rs) seed ONCE into the durable exclusion_list table at startup, where they are user-disableable/deletable and never resurrect. This key stays empty — the seed is code-defined, not settings-defined. Onboarding detect-and-suggest still runs on top.
